comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body: For an event-window forward test, how are the simulated fills generated when there is no broker connection? Recording a live alert timestamp is useful, but a midpoint or candle-price fill can still miss the spread and execution gap you want to measure. Showing quote age, bid/ask, assumed fill delay and the fill rule separately would make the comparison easier to interpret. QATS team here; interested in the execution assumptions rather than the event direction.

replies.author: aureliaspes
replies.body:
Good question. Here's how fills work today.

Forward testing in Aurelia Spes is built to answer one thing first: do your live signals behave like your backtest's? Each alert is booked as a paper trade at the price it carries, and the stop, daily loss cap and drawdown kill switch run on every price after that. No broker, no API keys, no money at risk.

That keeps signal drift clean and measurable on its own. Execution cost around an event (spread, quote age, fill delay) is a separate layer on top. In the backtest we already charge fees and slippage on both sides of every fill, and a signal on bar i fills at the open of bar i+1.

Splitting quote age, bid/ask, assumed delay and fill rule into their own fields is on our radar. Keeping signal error and execution error apart is exactly how we think about it.

If QATS wants to put a strategy through it, the first Backtest Lab run is free: [aureliaspes.com](http://aureliaspes.com)
